summary: DarkSide ransomware dropper/packer. The sample is a heavily packed PE (61KB) with only 1 static import (ExitProcess), RWX .text section, and high entropy indicating runtime unpacking. CAPA confirms XOR encoding (T1027) and aPLib decompression. YARA matched kernel32 PEB-walking API resolution technique. FLOSS extracted 191 strings but all are garbage/encoded with zero decoded strings, confirming heavy obfuscation. The filename is explicitly 'darkside.ex'. Code signing certificate ('OASIS COURT LIMITED', valid 2020-2021) is trivially forged and not evidence of legitimacy. Debug timestamp 2021-02-16 aligns with DarkSide ransomware operational timeline (pre-Colonial Pipeline attack).
key_evidence: Filename: darkside.ex — explicit DarkSide ransomware naming
Ghidra imports: Only 1 import (ExitProcess from KERNEL32.DLL) — extreme import minimalism indicates packer stub
Ghidra memory_blocks: .text section is RWX (Read+Write+Execute) with size 33792 — classic unpacking indicator
Malcat layout: .text entropy 225/256, .rsrc entropy 226/256 — high entropy indicates packed/encrypted payload
CAPA: 'encode data using XOR' (MITRE T1027 Defense Evasion, MBC E1027.m02)
CAPA: 'decompress data using aPLib' (MBC C0025.003) — confirms packer is aPLib-based
YARA: maldoc_find_kernel32_base_method_1 at offset 35465 — PEB walking for dynamic API resolution
YARA: HasOverlay triggered — overlay data present
YARA: HasDigitalSignature at offset 53760 — signed with Sectigo cert for OASIS COURT LIMITED
FLOSS: 191 strings extracted, 0 decoded, 0 stack strings — all strings are obfuscated/garbage
FLOSS: FindNextFileW string present — file enumeration capability for ransomware target discovery
Malcat metadata: Certificate issued to OASIS COURT LIMITED, valid 2020-12-21 to 2021-12-16 — forged/stolen cert
Malcat metadata: Debug date 2021-02-16 — aligns with DarkSide ransomware active period
Ghidra function_metrics: FUN_0040a135 has 46 blocks, cyclomatic complexity 23 — complex obfuscated unpacker logic
Ghidra: .text1 stub section (1024 bytes, RX) — small unpacker stub that decompresses main payload into .text
Speakeasy: No API calls logged — packer uses anti-emulation to evade sandbox analysis
